sampling_model.design: Dominated i.i.d. observed-data experiment on a deliberately restricted bounded likelihood-ratio chart, with square-root-density transports to fixed Hilbert spaces, norm-continuous operators, fixed rank labels, and a uniform positive reduced minimum modulus. The chart is not claimed to be Hellinger-open or to preserve the unrestricted dominated tangent set.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment \(A_i\in\{0,1\}\). The main target is an observed joint-bridge functional; its ATE interpretation requires the separate latent-extension proposition.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-bridge existence is a genuine observed solvability restriction. No injectivity, surjectivity, bridge uniqueness, completeness of an observed operator, or minimum-norm representative is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted penalized-minimax or Galerkin learning of rectangular outcome--treatment bridge grids; fold-specific pure and four-corner contrasts; an explicit positive-ridge training Gram/cross-moment solution; and a deterministic scalar affine-weight map under approximation, fourth-moment, Gram, ridge, coefficient-envelope, and mixed-bias rates.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 3, 6, and 7 give valid pair-specific doubly robust scores and regular asymptotically linear inference for selected nonunique inverse-problem nuisance limits.

Theorem 3.4 gives a root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear estimator with a selected nonunique bridge representative, and Corollary B.1 gives local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity.
Theorem 3 derives the efficient influence function and efficiency bound for the outcome-bridge-only negative-control observed model through a generalized inverse.
Theorem 3.1 identifies the proximal doubly robust score as efficient on the unique-bridge, surjective-operator submodel.
Theorem 1 gives efficient increasing-moment joint GMM inference when the outcome bridge has a uniquely determined finite-dimensional index.
Theorem 7 establishes local semiparametric efficiency for long-term data combination under unique bridges and an additional regularity condition.
Theorems 2.1--2.4 derive efficiency bounds for identified linear functionals when the NPIV regression itself is not identified.

body.tldr: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already gives root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear nonunique-bridge estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity, and BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified gives regular selected-pair inference. The new kernel concerns the local observed-law intersection in which outcome and treatment bridges must remain simultaneously solvable while both fibers may be non-singleton. On an explicit transported bounded likelihood-ratio fixed-rank closed-range chart, operator perturbation derives kernel and cokernel projection continuity, but score-lifting completeness for the actual restricted path class remains the load-bearing open obligation; only conditional on that result does the affine-hull projection become the canonical gradient and global bound across bridge pairs. A positive \(36\)-cell chart proves tangent equality locally, yields an exact strict Zhang--Bennett selected-pair gap, and gives an assumption-matched strict projection gap from ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification's outcome-only model. An explicitly fold-indexed ridge/Galerkin construction and primitive sieve, bridge-rate, Gram, envelope, and mixed-bias conditions imply learned efficient-signal convergence and feasible Wald inference. The main target is an observed joint-bridge functional; a separate latent-extension proposition identifies it with the ATE.

project_justification.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already establishes root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear nonunique-bridge estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity, BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified establishes regular selected-pair inference, and ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification computes efficiency in the outcome-bridge-only observed model. None characterizes the complete tangent closure of the joint observed-law intersection where outcome and treatment bridges remain simultaneously solvable, or its global canonical gradient across both nonunique fibers.
project_justification.niche: Treatment-bridge solvability can shrink the observed tangent space beyond the outcome-only model. Its nonredundant adjoint-solvability and null-interaction normals create an exact efficiency gain while preserving bridge nonuniqueness and avoiding a preferred representative.
project_justification.fill: The project defines an explicit transported bounded likelihood-ratio rank chart, derives projection continuity from operator perturbation, and keeps reverse score lifting for the actual restricted path class open rather than assuming it. Conditional on that obligation it derives the joint quotient gradient and attainment criterion; finite positive charts prove local submanifold status and exact Zhang--Bennett and Chen--Xie variance gaps, and a fully fold-indexed ridge construction with primitive learning conditions yields the affine-ensemble limit law.

body.related_work: MiaoGengTchetgen2018Proxy supplies the latent proximal conditions used only for the separate causal-identification proposition. ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness Theorem \(3.4\) already constructs a root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear estimator with nonunique bridges, and Corollary \(B.1\) establishes local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity; the new claim is confined to complete tangent and normal geometry and global across-pair efficiency for the simultaneous-existence observed-law model. BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified Theorem \(3\) gives the all-pair mixed-bias identity and Theorems \(6\)--\(7\) give the penalized-minimax selected-limit inference architecture; the exact finite chart shows that a Zhang--Bennett selected-pair variance can strictly exceed the joint affine quotient bound without questioning validity or local efficiency in their maintained model. ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification Theorem \(3\) gives the generalized-inverse canonical gradient for the outcome-bridge-only negative-control model. The assumption-matched comparison nests the joint model inside that transported outcome-only model and identifies the added adjoint-solvability normals, with exact variance gap \(1303968/66805375\) at the positive witness. CuiEtAl2024SemiparametricProximal Theorem \(3.1\) is the unique-and-surjective endpoint. SeveriniTripathi2012EfficiencyBounds supplies the quotient-functional precedent, and ChenSantos2018Overidentification supplies the range-versus-annihilator framework. AiChen2012SequentialMoments informs Gram stabilization and sieve weighting. AiShan2025EfficientProximalATE informs increasing-moment implementation but maintains a uniquely indexed bridge. ImbensEtAl2025LongTerm concerns a distinct unique-bridge data-combination model. BennettEtAl2023SourceConditionDR supplies primitive inverse-problem residual and product-rate tools.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The reverse inclusion \(\mathcal T_P\supseteq\mathcal C_P^\perp\) is not an assumption and is not implied by differentiating either bridge equation or by the operator-perturbation lemma. It requires scores of actual DQM paths in the intersection of the two solvability loci, with transported moving kernels, a shared \((W,X)\) marginal, and the bounded likelihood-ratio restriction maintained along each path. The deliberately restricted chart is not Hellinger-open and does not preserve the unrestricted dominated tangent set; generic dominated DQM paths with uncontrolled likelihood ratios are outside this version. Verifiable chart regimes include a positive finite-support simplex away from its boundary, including the \(36\)-cell witness, and a nonfinite bounded exponential-tilt family with bounded statistics on a small compact parameter set. The general treatment-solvability locus is not called a submanifold; submanifold status is proved only on the finite positive chart through the displayed Schur-complement constraint map and its full-row-rank Jacobian. Separate square integrability of \(Y\), \(h\), and \(q\) does not ensure square integrability of their score product. Closed range excludes generic compact infinite-rank problems. The exact finite witness verifies the Chen--Xie hypotheses and strict gap, but general strictness requires nonzero additional normal projection. The final Bennett publisher text remained inaccessible with an HTTP \(403\) response on 2026-09-13, so that comparison uses the public manuscript plus publisher metadata.
body.honest_scope: The field-tier contribution requires both the general score-lifting theorem relative to the deliberately restricted bounded-ratio path class and the primitive learned-projection theorem. Until reverse score lifting is proved, the general affine projection is a candidate and every general efficiency result is explicitly conditional; the finite positive chart has an unconditional tangent calculation. The chart covers finite-support laws uniformly away from the simplex boundary and bounded exponential-tilt families with bounded statistics, but not generic dominated DQM models or paths with uncontrolled likelihood ratios. The main statistical target is the observed joint-bridge functional. It equals the causal ATE only under the separately stated latent consistency, exchangeability, positivity, negative-control, and bridge-compatibility conditions. Rank-boundary adaptation, generic compact ill-posed operators, and a full SUPPORT reanalysis remain outside scope. Under unique bijective bridge operators, the result reduces to Cui et al.'s efficient score.
